svg.title: THE ust CLI — ONE ENTRYPOINT, THE WHOLE SURFACE
svg.desc: The ust CLI — one entrypoint, the whole command surface (parsed from the real binary’s help). Install with npm i -g @ust-protocol/cli. The 13 subcommands: verify <file|-> (verify a transcript — exit 0 = VALID, 1 = not (--require-anchored demands proven time)); canon <file|-> (print canonical bytes + hash — diff another language's implementation against this); stream <frames…> (a verdict about a RANGE, not one document: chain · forks · completeness (--checkpoint is what makes completeness answerable at all)); forkchoice <docs…> (pick the CANONICAL document among candidates for ONE ust_id — the anchor decides, never the candidates themselves); discovery <domain> (probe a domain's serving surface and report an honest verdict — any infrastructure); genesis --domain <d> (run the HIGH genesis ceremony (add --publish cf for one-click serving)); key add --domain <d> --root <enc> --role <data|issuance> (ADD a key BESIDE the current one (never replaces it)); rotate --domain <d> --root <enc> (APPEND a key rotation to the served log (never re-mints — documents signed by the old key stay valid)); cadence --domain <d> --root <enc> --seconds <n> --effective-from <slot> ( DECLARE the signed grid your stream follows — what completeness is measured against); reroot --domain <d> --ca-key <enc> (RE-ROOT onto a new genesis, crossing EVERY genesis-rooted structure you run — key-log, authority chain, witness log (the NAME), cadence. Writes artifacts; publishes nothing. Your writer must cross the last axis itself.); publish <cf|self> --domain <d> --genesis <f> (serve an existing genesis: cf deploys the adapter, self writes the four artifacts for YOUR stack (asked if omitted)); mirror <domain> (publish and attest a SECOND-vendor copy, so your identity does not rest on one provider); witness rekor --domain <d> (log the genesis in a public transparency log, so a second published history cannot go unnoticed). Exit 0 = VALID with the tier in the verdict, 1 = not; the ceremony self-verifies its outputs, fail-closed.

g.text: THE ust CLI — ONE ENTRYPOINT, THE WHOLE SURFACE
# 13 subcommands — this table is parsed from the real help
verify a transcript — exit 0 = VALID, 1 = not (--require-anchored demands proven time)
print canonical bytes + hash — diff another language's implementation against this
a verdict about a RANGE, not one document: chain · forks · completeness (--checkpoint is what makes completeness answerable at all)
pick the CANONICAL document among candidates for ONE ust_id — the anchor decides, never the candidates themselves
probe a domain's serving surface and report an honest verdict — any infrastructure
run the HIGH genesis ceremony (add --publish cf for one-click serving)
ADD a key BESIDE the current one (never replaces it)
APPEND a key rotation to the served log (never re-mints — documents signed by the old key stay valid)
DECLARE the signed grid your stream follows — what completeness is measured against

RE-ROOT onto a new genesis, crossing EVERY genesis-rooted structure you run — key-log, authority chain, witness log (the NAME), cadence. Writes artifacts; publishes nothing. Your writer must cross the last axis itself.
serve an existing genesis: cf deploys the adapter, self writes the four artifacts for YOUR stack (asked if omitted)
publish and attest a SECOND-vendor copy, so your identity does not rest on one provider
log the genesis in a public transparency log, so a second published history cannot go unnoticed
exit 0 = VALID (tier in the verdict) · 1 = not · the ceremony self-verifies its outputs — fail-closed
